_note:
Return in a MULTILINE field, decided once for every renderer.

A single-line `<textfield>` has an unambiguous Return: there is nothing to insert, so it
submits, and `on:submit` has always worked there. `<textarea>` had no submit at all, and the
composer that needed one (an AI prompt box) is the most common multiline field there is.

The reason it is not simply "Return submits" is that Return already MEANS something in a
multiline field, and on a phone soft keyboard it should keep meaning it: a newline. Enter-to-send
is a HARDWARE-keyboard convention - web, desktop, an iPad or tablet with a keyboard attached - and
the platform's own chat apps agree, which is why every one of them still shows a send button on
the phone. So this grammar decides a HARDWARE key event and never touches the soft keyboard.

The rules, in the order they are applied:

  1. Not a Return key at all -> `ignore`. The field keeps whatever the key already did.
  2. Shift or Alt held -> `newline`, ALWAYS, and before anything else. These are the two chords
     every editor on every platform uses to mean "I want a line break here", and an author who
     turns Enter-to-send on must not take them away.
  3. The primary modifier (Cmd on Apple, Ctrl elsewhere) -> `submit` when a handler is bound.
     This is the universal send chord; it is never ambiguous, so it works whether or not the
     author asked for Enter-to-send.
  4. Bare Return -> `submit` only when the author wrote `submitOnEnter` AND a handler is bound.
  5. Anything else -> `newline`.

`ignore` and `newline` are deliberately DIFFERENT answers. `ignore` means this grammar has no
opinion and the renderer must not consume the event; `newline` means Return was handled and
resolved to inserting a break. A renderer that collapses the two will eat keystrokes it was
never asked about.

With no `on:submit` bound, nothing here can ever return `submit` - a field cannot swallow a
Return into a handler that does not exist.

cases.name: a bare Return is a newline by default
submitOnEnter makes a bare Return send
submitOnEnter with nothing bound still cannot send
Shift+Return is a newline even with submitOnEnter
Alt+Return is a newline even with submitOnEnter
Cmd+Return sends without submitOnEnter - the universal chord
Ctrl+Return sends too: cmd is the PRIMARY modifier, not the Apple one
Cmd+Return with no handler is ignored, never swallowed
Cmd+Shift+Return is a newline: the explicit break chord wins
Cmd+Alt+Return is a newline for the same reason
Return is the key on every toolkit spelling
any other key is not this grammar's business
Escape is not this grammar's business either
an empty key name decides nothing
